question: Which of the following members of the homologous series of alkanes has the highest melting point?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C4H10.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **hydrocarbon butane (C4H10)** is non-polar.
 
• Due to the negligible difference in **electronegativity **between the bonds connecting **carbon **and **hydrogen**, the molecule as a whole lacks a **dipole moment**.
 
• Purely non-polar compounds show **dispersion forces**, which become stronger with increasing **molar mass**.
 
• These forces are based on electron orbits, which momentarily produce **positive **and **negative ends**, or dipoles, in the molecule.
 
• More electrons will be present in a molecule with a greater **molar **mass, which will result in **stronger dispersion **forces since the temporary dipoles will be more pronounced.
 
• Because butane has **stronger dispersion forces **and needs more heat energy to overcome them, it has a **higher melting **and **boiling** **point**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• A collection of chemicals known as a **homologous series **differ only in the length of the **carbon chain **but have the same general formula.
 
• There is often a shared set of functional groups among molecules in a homologous series, leading to **identical** **chemical **and **physical properties**.
 
• **Alkane** homologous series like **CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈,** etc. are an example.
 
• They diverge from one another in terms of **-CH₂** **units**.
